>_ Episode 7 · Aug 20, 2026 · 1h 43m

Computer Minds, Mike Levin & Panpsychism

Play Episode 7 on YouTube
Watch on YouTube SpotifyApple Podcasts

In this episode of Philosophy, Programs, and Prompts, Casey Hart (@OntologyExplained) and Carl Brown(@InternetOfBugs) dive deep into biologist Michael Levin’s provocative claims about cognition in basic computer algorithms. Does a distributed bubble sort display "delayed gratification" or proto-cognitive desires? Or are these emergent properties simply artifacts of velocity differences, ill-defined terms, and after-the-fact p-hacking?

Casey and Carl break down the computer science, philosophical frameworks (substrate independence, Platonic spaces, and supervenience), and the importance of rigorous, falsifiable hypothesis testing when crossing disciplinary boundaries.
